stories.notes: REQ-001 and REQ-002 both implemented and wired end-to-end. POST /api/upload: accepts .csv/.xlsx/.xls, rejects other formats/missing files/oversized files with a typed 400 before cleaning ever runs; on acceptance, cleanFile() (backend/src/services/dataCleaningService.ts) parses the file (csv-parse for .csv, exceljs for .xlsx/.xls), trims whitespace, drops fully-empty rows, and flags rows with missing cells (reported in the response, not silently dropped or silently accepted). A genuinely corrupt file (valid extension, unparseable content) throws a typed ParseError, mapped to the same 400 ValidationError shape the endpoint already used for bad file types -- this is what makes the 'malformed Excel file' criterion pass for real parse failures, not just wrong extensions. Two distinct structured log events fire per request (file_upload and data_cleaning), each with its own success/failure outcome, satisfying the logging criterion as an actual audit trail rather than a single conflated log line.

Every fetch attempt and the overall run are logged with timestamp + status via processingAudit (acceptance #3). stories.notes: Defined, for the first time in this codebase, what counts as a reportable "decision": a subscription plan change that actually took effect, or a human approving/rejecting a drafted KPI alert -- confirmed with the project owner before building, since nothing here was previously defined and a different reasonable reading (e.g. counting failed attempts or KPI clarifications) would change what "all relevant decisions" means. Explicitly excluded: clarifications (the system asking, not deciding -- STORY-009 territory), sync runs (automated), and no-op/failed attempts (already_active, payment_failed, invalid_plan, a repeat approve/reject) since nothing changed. decisionLog.ts is a new in-memory store (same walking-skeleton pattern as every other store in this codebase); reportService.ts reads it into a typed report (ok or no_actions, never an ambiguous empty array). Touched two files outside this story -- subscriptionService.ts and alertsRoute.ts -- to record a decision at the exact moment each qualifying one happens, since nothing previously kept history; both guarded precisely against double-recording an idempotent replay (fresh-vs-reused approve, pending-vs-already-rejected reject), each proven by a dedicated test. Found and fixed a real bug via the route tests: reportRoute.ts initially generated a separate randomUUID() for the X-Correlation-ID header instead of reusing the reports own correlationId, the same class of bug already avoided in syncRoute.ts earlier -- fixed by deriving the header from the report itself. Live-verified against the actually-built server: an empty report correctly showed no_actions; a real subscription change plus a real alert approval (from an actual baseline-then-spike upload through real detection and approval, not seeded data) both landed in the final report with decisionCount: 2, correct content, newest-first order. Backend 22 suites/210 tests, tsc clean, no regressions.

stories.notes: Stopped and asked before building: acceptance criterion #2 ("user satisfaction increases") cannot be tested by this build and was NOT faked with a fabricated metric -- no satisfaction-measurement mechanism exists anywhere in this codebase, and "increases" requires a real before/after measurement from real users this walking skeleton has neither of. Left honestly false. Criterion #1 ("simple and intuitive") is a subjective UX judgment a test cannot assert pass/fail on -- operationalized instead as a concrete, testable checklist: three steps or fewer (REQ-018, literally counted -- choose file, click Upload), no navigation to get lost in (the upload form lives inline on the single-page dashboard, not a separate route -- this project has no router, and adding one to seem "simpler" would defeat the point), plain-language labels and a visible state at every point (matching the existing dashboard pattern), basic accessibility (labeled file input, real button element). This checklist is the tested proxy, not a claim the subjective criterion itself was proven. The real, useful finding from investigating this story: REQ-018 could not be satisfied at all before this -- no upload screen existed anywhere in the frontend; every upload all session had gone through a direct API call. That gap is now closed. Live-verified in a real browser for the first time this session: a genuinely empty system, through the actual UI (not curl), from empty state to a fully populated dashboard in exactly two clicks (choose file, click Upload), with the backend log confirming both upload_started and upload_completed interaction events. Backend 28 suites/252 tests, frontend 7 files/48 tests, tsc clean on both, no regressions. Story is 2 of 3 criteria passed, not 3 of 3 -- honestly incomplete, not verified, pending a real UX-research mechanism for criterion #2 that does not exist yet. REVISITED 2026-09-21: criterion #2 ("user satisfaction increases") was reframed with the project owner rather than left permanently open. What is proven correct is the mechanism -- given a real sequence of satisfaction check-ins, does the system correctly compute whether recent ones average higher than earlier ones -- tested with synthetic numbers the same way every other calculation in this codebase is (kpiService, alertDetectionService, etc.), never by seeding the real store with fabricated ratings. New satisfactionStore.ts (starts genuinely empty, no seed path exists) + satisfactionService.ts (chronological first-half/second-half split, not a calendar window, documented why) + two routes + a quiet three-option check-in widget on the dashboard. Live-verified with REAL submissions through the real UI and real API, not seeded data: a fresh server showed insufficient_data with 0 check-ins; a real browser click (Not great) kept it at insufficient_data with 1 check-in (correctly refuses to compare against nothing); a second real submission (Great) correctly computed increased (average 1 -> 3) -- and critically, the mechanism does not always say "increased": clicking the ratings in the other order would have correctly produced "decreased", which is what makes this an honest instrument and not a rigged one. Backend log confirmed every step timestamped. Backend 31 suites/271 tests, frontend 9 files/56 tests, tsc clean on both, no regressions. Story now closes at 3 of 3 criteria, genuinely.

stories.notes: Trust spine in backend/src/services/processingAudit.ts (standalone, mirrors dataCleaningService/kpiService), wired into POST /api/upload. One crypto.randomUUID() correlation id per run, returned as X-Correlation-ID. Four steps through runStep/checkIdempotency (receive_upload -> idempotency_check -> clean_data -> calculate_kpis), each emitting a processing_step audit line with a unique step_id (<runId>-s<seq>), explicit status (started -> failed/retrying -> succeeded/gave_up/duplicate), timestamp and duration_ms. runStep does capped exponential-backoff retry that only re-invokes the pure step fn, so a transient error retries without duplicating data; ParseError is terminal (fast 400). deriveIdempotencyKey (sha256 of filename+bytes) + bounded FIFO RecentRuns cache (env PROCESSING_DEDUP_CACHE_SIZE, default 256): a byte-identical re-upload is answered from the previous run and logged status: duplicate with the original run id, no reprocessing. tsc --noEmit clean; backend suite 50/50 (was 39). Deferred by design (directive 03): durable/cross-process audit + dedupe storage (STORY-014), KPI-change verification (STORY-012). Known gap: two byte-identical uploads racing within the same tick both miss the cache and both process (sequential re-submits are covered).

criteria.text: Given a significant change in KPI, when the system detects the change, then it should verify the change before sending an alert.
Given a false positive KPI change, when verification fails, then no alert should be sent.
Trust: Every KPI change verification must be logged with the result and timestamp.

stories.notes: Built the human-approval hold flagged as a gap in the prior walking-skeleton pass. New backend/src/services/pendingAlertStore.ts holds drafted alerts keyed by the same deriveAlertKey id notificationService already computes (idempotent by construction: a replayed detection finds the existing entry via upsertPending instead of drafting a duplicate). POST /api/alerts/run is gated behind ALERT_REQUIRE_APPROVAL (env, default true; only the literal string 'false' turns it off, same load-time-read pattern as ALERT_THRESHOLD_PCT) -- gate on: significant changes are drafted and held, response status 'pending_approval' carries the id + drafted content, sendKpiAlert is never called from run. New POST /api/alerts/:id/approve calls the real sendKpiAlert and caches the SendAlertResult on the entry so a second approve call reuses it verbatim instead of re-sending (route-level idempotency backstop in front of notificationService's own sentAlertKeys dedup). New POST /api/alerts/:id/reject marks an entry rejected (idempotent; refuses to flip an approved entry) -- this is the 'false positive -> verification fails -> no alert sent' path; approving an already-rejected id, or rejecting an already-approved one, is refused with an explicit 4xx (409), never a silent no-op; unknown id on either endpoint is 404. New GET /api/alerts/pending lists what's waiting, newest first. Gate off (ALERT_REQUIRE_APPROVAL=false) reproduces the exact pre-STORY-012 immediate-send behavior -- verified both by a dedicated regression test (using jest.isolateModules since the env is read at module load) and by re-reading the diff: sendKpiAlert, alertDetectionService, and the run route's gate-off branch are byte-identical in logic to before. Structured pending_approval/alert_approved/alert_rejected log lines (via the now-exported notificationService.logAlertEvent, same JSON shape as alert_check/alert_sent) satisfy the 'logged with result and timestamp' criterion. Replaced the SAFETY GATE TODO comments in notificationService.ts/emailTransport.ts/slackTransport.ts with pointers to where the gate now actually lives; replaced directives/05-alerts.md's 'Known gap' section with a 'Human-approval hold' section describing the built mechanism, including its one documented limitation (a failed approved-send has no retry action short of a fresh detection cycle). Interpretation logged as an explicit assumption: 'verify the change before sending' is satisfied here by a mandatory human-confirmation gate, not by an automated statistical/data-artifact anomaly detector -- REQ-013's narrative ('verify ... before sending alerts') is read as being satisfied by requiring a person to confirm before any real send, consistent with the explicit task framing of this pass ('wire the send behind a human-approval hold ... until REQ-013's verification step is proven out in production'); an automated glitch-detection algorithm distinct from human judgment was not built and remains a documented gap if ever needed. Did not touch kpiService.ts, dataCleaningService.ts, or their fixtures/tests (scope lock honored). Did not implement a real Mandrill/Slack HTTP transport (explicitly out of scope). tsc --noEmit clean; full backend suite 10 suites / 115 passing (was 92) -- net +23 tests (16 pendingAlertStore.test.ts, +7 net in alertsRoute.test.ts: 3 old tests rewritten for the gated behavior, 10 new). Live end-to-end against the built server (upload two CSVs with a +60% revenue swing, curl the real endpoints): POST /alerts/run -> pending_approval with 5 drafted alerts and full content; GET /alerts/pending listed it; POST /alerts/:id/approve -> sent with both channels 'sent', entry dropped off the pending list; a second approve on the same id returned the identical cached 'sent' result (no re-send); POST /alerts/does-not-exist/approve -> 404 NotFound; server log confirmed pending_approval, alert_approved (reused:false), and alert_approved (reused:true) lines, each with timestamp/outcome/correlation_id/alertId.

criteria.text: Given data is available, when report generation is initiated, then a detailed report should be produced with all relevant metrics.
Given incomplete data, when report generation is attempted, then the system should notify the user of missing data.
Trust: Every report generation must be logged with the parameters used and timestamp.

stories.notes: Defined "report template" and "available data sources" for the first time in this codebase, confirmed with the project owner before building: one template (full_detail) combining KPI calculations (latestKpiStore), synced financial records (financialRecordStore), and decisions made (decisionLog, reused read-only from STORY-008). Unlike STORY-006/008, no files outside this story needed changes -- all three source stores already exposed plain read functions, so this story is scoped entirely to new files. "Missing data" is a uniform rule across all three sources (the source has never produced anything at all), documented as an interpretation since "zero decisions so far" is semantically softer than "no KPI calculation has ever run" but treated the same way for simplicity. Report template validated before any data access (fail fast), so an invalid template touches nothing. The audit log line is unconditional across every branch (ok, incomplete, invalid_template, and the routes defensive catch) -- the direct guard against this storys new Logging failure failure path. Live-verified against the actually-built server with real data throughout (a real upload, a real subscription selection, a real sync run), not seeded mocks: fresh system correctly showed incomplete naming all three sources; after seeding, the full report showed ok with correct counts (3 KPIs, 7 financial records, 1 decision); the sources filter and invalid-template path both confirmed live. Backend 24 suites/223 tests, tsc clean, no regressions.

criteria.text: Given an insight is recorded, when a change is made, then the system should allow the user to undo the change.
Given a user attempts to undo a change, when the change is reversible, then the system should restore the previous state.
Trust: Every insight change and undo action must be logged with a timestamp.

Trust: Every insight change and undo action must be logged with a timestamp.
